//====================================================
// launch.json
//
// VS Code debugger configuration for the TingoBingo project.
//
// This file tells VS Code:
// - which executable to run
// - which debugger to use (GDB)
// - where the program starts
// - which build task to run before debugging
//
// Note: Standard JSON does not support comments, so this
// explanation is kept outside the file.
//====================================================
What each setting does
Setting	Purpose
"version": "0.2.0"	Version of the VS Code launch configuration format.
"configurations"	List of available debugging configurations.
"name": "Debug Template"	Name shown in VS Code's Run and Debug menu.
"type": "cppdbg"	Uses the Microsoft C/C++ debugger extension.
"request": "launch"	Launch a new program rather than attaching to one that's already running.
"program"	The executable that will be started (build/TingoBingo.exe).
"args"	Command-line arguments passed to the program. Empty means none.
"stopAtEntry": false	Begin execution immediately instead of stopping at main().
"cwd"	Current working directory when the program starts.
"environment"	Environment variables supplied to the program.
"externalConsole": true	Opens a separate console window for the program.
"MIMode": "gdb"	Specifies that GDB is the debugger.
"miDebuggerPath"	Location of the GDB executable installed with MSYS2.
"preLaunchTask": "Build"	Runs the VS Code Build task before starting the debugger.
===========================================================================================

//====================================================
// settings.json
//
// Workspace settings for the TingoBingo project.
//
// These settings tell the C/C++ extension:
// - which compiler is being used
// - where project header files are located
//
// Note: JSON does not support comments, so this
// explanation is kept outside the file.
//====================================================
What each setting does
Setting	Purpose
"C_Cpp.default.compilerPath"	Tells the C/C++ extension which compiler to use for IntelliSense 
and code analysis. Here it points to the MSYS2 MinGW-w64 g++ compiler.

"C_Cpp.default.includePath"	Lists folders that contain header (.h) files so IntelliSense 
can find them.

"${workspaceFolder}/include"	Includes the project's main include directory.

"${workspaceFolder}/include/**"	Includes all subfolders within include, allowing headers 
to be organized into folders without additional configuration.
Why this file matters

Without these settings, VS Code may:

Show false "Cannot open source file" errors.
Fail to autocomplete your classes and functions.
Be unable to jump to definitions or provide accurate IntelliSense.

This file doesn't affect how your program is compiled by g++; it mainly
 helps the VS Code C/C++ extension understand your project structure while you're editing.

=========================================================================

//====================================================
// tasks.json
//
// Defines build tasks that can be run from VS Code.
//
// This project uses an MSYS2 shell to execute the
// build script, which compiles the TingoBingo source
// code into an executable.
//
// Note: JSON does not support comments, so this
// explanation is kept outside the file.
//====================================================
What each setting does
Setting	Purpose
"version": "2.0.0"	Version of the VS Code Tasks configuration format.
"tasks"	List of tasks available in the project.
"label": "Build"	The name of the task. This is the task that launch.json runs before 
debugging.
"type": "process"	Runs an external program rather than a shell command directly.
"command"	Starts the MSYS2 shell (msys2_shell.cmd).
"args"	Arguments passed to the MSYS2 shell to control how it starts.
MSYS2 arguments
Argument	Purpose
-defterm	Uses the default terminal.
-no-start	Runs in the current terminal instead of opening a new MSYS2 window.
-mingw64	Starts the MinGW 64-bit environment so g++ and Raylib are available.
-here	Starts MSYS2 in the project folder.
-c	Executes the following command and then exits.
Build command
cd "${workspaceFolder}" && ./scripts/build.sh

This command:

Changes into the project folder.
Runs your build.sh script.
The script compiles all of TingoBingo.
Produces build/TingoBingo.exe.
Remaining settings
Setting	Purpose
"group"	Marks this as the project's default build task. Pressing Ctrl+Shift+B runs it
 automatically.
"problemMatcher": "$gcc"	Parses g++ compiler output so errors and warnings appear 
in VS Code's Problems panel and can be clicked to jump directly to the relevant line of code.

I really like this setup because it keeps everything simple:

Ctrl + Shift + B
        │
        ▼
VS Code Task
        │
        ▼
MSYS2 Shell
        │
        ▼
build.sh
        │
        ▼
g++
        │
        ▼
TingoBingo.exe

That flow is exactly how your project gets built every time.
